title: Why SEC is now 'not sure' it can take legal action vs LSU | Report
description: The latest update on the SEC's lawsuit against LSU as the eligibility crisis continues to rock college sports.
fullText:
The SEC's legal battle against Louisiana State remains at a standstill, and when the next move may happen seems to get farther and farther away.

ESPN college football insider Pete Thamel reported on "College GameDay" on Saturday, Sept. 12, that the SEC is "monitoring things right now" as "they're not sure they can take action against LSU because of that state court order in Louisiana."

Thamel did not go into specifics about the aforementioned state court order.

However, earlier this month, when East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden issued a preliminary injunction making it possible for LSU to roster players who had signed NFL contracts, the court order also barred the SEC from punishing LSU for playing those athletes.

The update comes after a federal hearing scheduled to take place at Hugo L. Black United States Courthouse in Birmingham on Wednesday, Sept. 9, was continued.

REQUIRED READING: Hearing in SEC suit against LSU postponed moments before Wednesday start

U.S. District Judge Annemarie Carney Axon was due to hear the SEC's request for a temporary restraining order against LSU, which was part of an amended complaint from the school, seeking protection against any retaliation that could result from decisions made during a specially-called meeting of SEC officials on Thursday, Sept. 10. Court filings described that the conference would vote on whether LSU should be expelled, but the conference shared a statement that afternoon indicating that the parties were working towards a resolution.

The scheduled 1 p.m. hearing was postponed and is expected to be rescheduled through a separate order. No reason for the delay was given.

The SEC filed suit against LSU on Thursday, Sept. 3, seeking preliminary and permanent injunctions tied to what it described as its First Amendment right of "expressive association" — in other words, the conference's argument that it cannot be forced to associate with a member acting contrary to its mission and values.

On the night before the scheduled Wednesday hearing, LSU rostered two other players to reach its 105-man roster limit, leaving no room for former NFL signees Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris.

Leading up to Sept. 9, Wright and Harris were granted preliminary injunctions allowing them to compete after initially receiving temporary restraining orders. The SEC argued that adding Wright and Harris would violate conference eligibility rules, and LSU's continued pursuit of their eligibility resulted in the conference's lawsuit.

The SEC filed an amended complaint on Tuesday, Sept. 8, seeking a temporary restraining order ahead of a Sept. 10 meeting of conference leaders, when LSU's membership in the league was expected to be considered, according to court filings.

In its filing, the SEC argued that having to associate with LSU would cause "irreparable harm" if the league were unable to distance its name, brand, championships and media properties from conduct it opposes.

Thamel's Saturday report indicates uncertainty over how the Louisiana court order continues to complicate what, if any, action the SEC can take against LSU while the federal case remains unresolved.

title: Trey Wingo, Bob Ley look back on hosting ‘SportsCenter’ on 9/11
description: Friday marked 25 years since the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Center, and across the sports world there were solemn remembrances as well as celebrations of the heroes that stepped up that day. Trey Wingo used the day to call up Bob Ley, with whom he hosted the 6 p.m. edition of SportsCenter…
fullText:
Friday marked 25 years since the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Center, and across the sports world there were solemn remembrances as well as celebrations of the heroes that stepped up that day.

Trey Wingo used the day to call up Bob Ley, with whom he hosted the 6 p.m. edition of SportsCenter on Tuesday, September 11, 2001, and look back on the surreal, traumatic, and life-changing day, and how they almost didn't go on with the show.

"As I'm driving into work that day I'm like, what am I even going to talk about today? What could remotely matter?" Wingo said. "I remember we got into the offices that day and everyone was sort of just thinking about what could we do, what's available, what's this. I was like, 'Hey maybe we should just turn over all of our resources to ABC News, give them everything.'"

Wingo remembered a meeting with Ley and producer Norby Williamson, where they discussed whether or not the show should air that night.

"I was like, I don't think we should do a show. I think it would be disrespectful. All this stuff. Because I was overwhelmed," Wingo said.

Ley was on the other side of the debate.

"I remember you sat dawn and said 'Look, here's what I think. Obviously this is a really traumatic day and we don't know what's going on, but our job as the show of record' — which is what we thought that the six o'clock SportsCenter was at that time, it was the show of record of what was going on in sports that day — you said, 'We need to chronicle this so people can understand, and have a benchmark to know what happened on that day.'"

Wingo concluded by admitting that Ley, and ultimately SportsCenter, made the right call to go on air.

"In hindsight, I was 100% wrong and you were 100% right."

From there, Ley and Wingo continue to share memories from the day itself and the days that followed, both confronting the strangeness that comes with watching something so visceral slowly become a piece of history.

They also remembered the sports moments that brought the country together in the aftermath of the attacks, namely President Bush's first pitch at Yankee Stadium and Mike Piazza's monster home run for the Mets.

title: Talarico says he 'missed the mark' as he backtracks on controversial woke statements
description: James Talarico now backs banning transgender surgeries for minors and opposing trans athletes in girls' sports as the Texas Senate race heats up.
fullText:
In a Fox News exclusive interview, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico came out in favor of banning gender surgery for minors and opposed transgender-identifying men competing in women's sports.

Talarico also backtracked on several of his more controversial claims, including saying there are six genders and that "God is nonbinary."

This comes as the Texas Senate race, which is surprisingly close according to recent Fox News polling, enters its final months. The race is considered critical to both parties' chances of securing a Senate majority. Talarico is facing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican who has faced controversies of his own. A Republican loss in Texas would significantly impact President Donald Trump's ability to implement his agenda.

Fox News spoke with Talarico at a food drive campaign event in Dallas on Tuesday. Talarico's event took place as the first-ever GOP midterm convention kicked off just miles away in downtown Dallas.

Talarico Campaigns With Surgeon Who Operated On Transgender Minors: 'Wolf In Sheep's Clothing'

Asked whether he would vote as a U.S. senator in favor of a national ban on gender surgery for minors, Talarico answered, "Absolutely."

He said, "I've been consistent on this issue," explaining his opposition to a Texas bill to ban transgender surgeries on minors by saying the measure "was overly broad."

"If you go back and check, I voted for a major amendment to limit the bill to banning surgeries for minors," he said. "As a lawmaker, my job is to try to sift through everything the bill does. And sometimes there's stuff in it that's really harmful, and I have no choice but to oppose the bill as a whole."

"It's why I try to use amendments, to narrow the focus of the bill so that it does exactly what we intend it to do," he continued. "It's what I tried to do with that piece of legislation, and unfortunately, the amendment I supported was unsuccessful."

In 2023, as a member of the Texas House of Representatives, Talarico voted against a state bill titled SB 14, which prohibited certain gender surgery, puberty blockers and certain hormone treatments for minors. There were 18 amendments to the bill proposed by Democrats, all of which Talarico voted in favor and all of which ultimately failed.

In the same interview, Talarico acknowledged that men in women's sports is a significant issue in Texas. He said, "I oppose trans athletes playing in girls' sports if it endangers safety or fairness."

"Every sport has to be safe and fair. As a former public school teacher, I care a lot about our student athletes. I care a lot about our students. And so, I will oppose trans athletes playing in girls' sports if it risks safety or fairness," he said.

Talarico's comments mark a shift from his earlier position as a Texas state lawmaker.

In 2021, while serving on the Texas House Public Education Committee, he opposed SB 29, which sought to require public-school athletes to compete based on the biological sex listed on their birth certificate, calling the issue a "manufactured problem." Later that year, he voted against HB 25, which enacted similar restrictions into Texas law.

James Talarico Admits Past Comments 'Missed The Mark' When Confronted On Claims Like God Is 'Non-binary'

He also addressed perhaps his most controversial statement, which he made in 2021, while opposing a Texas bill to keep men out of women's sports. Talarico said on the state House floor that "God is both masculine and feminine and everything in between. God is non-binary."

"I was being provocative with that statement. I get that," Talarico admitted, explaining, "What I was trying to say is that you can't use human categories to define God, and that's not controversial theologically. In fact, the late Charlie Kirk, the late Pope Benedict all said the same thing."

Talarico continued, claiming "these comments are being clipped out of context to try to distract from Ken Paxton's career of corruption."

"You mentioned [Paxton] being acquitted in the state Senate. That was after two of his billionaire megadonors gave the lieutenant governor a $3 million check to buy his acquittal," Talarico said. "So, Ken Paxton is the most corrupt politician in Texas, and he's gonna try to clip some of my comments, including comments where I was being a little provocative in order to try to distract from that career."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Paxton campaign for a response.

Longtime Gop Aide Defects To Dem Rising Star As Texas Senate Battle For Cornyn's Seat Heats Up

Regarding his past comment about there being more than two genders, Talarico said he does not currently believe there are six sexes.

"I've missed the mark on some of my past statements. I will be the first to admit it," he said. "What I meant is that there are two sexes, and then there's a small percentage of people with genetic abnormalities."

"Obviously didn't say it correctly. There are not six sexes. There are two, and I think the reason that politicians in that convention center across the street want to talk about six sexes is because they don't want to talk about $6 diesel," he said.

Though he walked back these controversies, Talarico did not hold back on his criticism of the Supreme Court, which he described as "infected" with corruption, saying it "needs to be overhauled."

He said that if elected, "You're going to expect that I will vote for overhaul to the Supreme Court. That will include binding codes of conduct for our justices. It'll include term limits, and I am open to a discussion about expanding the number of justices."

Following these controversies, Talarico pledged to keep his message focused on affordability for the remainder of the campaign.

"Everywhere I go across the state of Texas, people are struggling to survive in this economy. They are struggling to afford the basics: groceries, gas, utilities, healthcare. And that's what I'm going to be focused on from now until Election Day."

On the topic of affordability, Talarico said that "we should not have a state income tax" in Texas. This is despite Talarico previously voting against a measure to permanently ban a state income tax, which he suggested was redundant and an example of "government waste at its worst."

The measure was ultimately passed by the Texas Legislature and approved by Texas voters in November 2019.

title: Why is there an NFL game in Australia?
description: The NFL has so far played regular-season games in seven international countries but this week's trip to Australia represents a new frontier for the USA's biggest sports league.
fullText:
The NFL has so far played regular-season games in seven international countries but this week's trip to Australia represents a new frontier.

It is the NFL's first game in the Asia-Pacific region, with the USA's biggest sports league making its longest-ever road trip for the first of a record nine international games in 2026.

It will take place about 10,000 miles from the NFL's New York headquarters, in front of about 100,000 fans at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground.

That means the Los Angeles Rams will 'host' the San Francisco 49ers on a more open oval field on Friday (01:35 BST).

But when NFL commissioner Roger Goodell visited the MCG for the first time in April, he said the historic arena "speaks to you", and it says "this is the right place to be".

American football is coming to Australia - can it succeed?

Live NFL games have been broadcast in Australia since 1995 and a pre-season exhibition game was held in Sydney in 1999.

Local interest has soared since 2022, though, when the NFL made the global growth of American football a strategic priority.

The league pivoted away from a potential overseas franchise to playing more games internationally. It has invested in new markets before deciding whether to take a game there, holding year-round events to build the fanbase.

Australian players Jordan Mailata (Philadelphia) and Michael Dickson (Seattle) have also captured the imagination down under, playing for the past two Super Bowl winners.

According to the league, the number of fans in Australia has nearly doubled since 2022 to 8.8 million - almost one in three of the country's entire population.

That includes those flooding to one of the world's fastest-growing sports, flag football - the non-contact version of American football.

The NFL played a big part in flag being approved for its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028 and has expanded the sport from 10 schools in Australia to more than 500.

Now it aims to help flag football secure a spot at Brisbane 2032, with NFL executive Peter O'Reilly acknowledging that is a key reason for playing in Australia.

Being a sports-mad country, Australia was always on the NFL's radar, and after testing long-distance logistics with trips to Brazil in 2024 and 2025, the league felt ready to head down under.

Sydney and Perth were in the running but Melbourne is regarded as the nation's sports capital and the MCG is the biggest stadium in the southern hemisphere.

A deal was announced in February 2025, during Super Bowl week, and while some fans expressed anger at ticket prices when they went on sale in April 2026, they sold out in minutes.

The state of Victoria is reportedly paying up to A$15m, external (£8m) for the right to host the game but expects one of the state's biggest returns. Dublin enjoyed a tenfold return on its investment to stage its first NFL game last September.

Almost 50% of the MCG tickets were bought by fans outside Victoria or overseas, so about 50,000 fans will visit Melbourne this week.

'The G' is also right next to Melbourne Park, home of tennis' Australian Open, an ideal venue for a three-day fan festival, which began with a watch party for last night's season opener.

The NFL picked this year's Super Bowl week to announce that the 49ers will be the Rams' opponents in Melbourne, which created a buzz in Australia and California.

Not only are the Rams and 49ers regular Super Bowl contenders but they are also divisional rivals in the ultra-competitive NFC West. In addition, there is heaps of hype around the Rams.

With this season's Super Bowl being held in LA, they have gone all-in to reach the big game. First they traded for defensive stars Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, which cemented them as championship favourites.

Then three-time defensive player of the year Aaron Donald returned from retirement and although the 35-year-old has not travelled to Australia, Garrett and McDuffie will both make their Rams debut at the MCG.

Fred Warner, Nick Bosa and George Kittle are set to return from injury for the 49ers, with Mike Evans making his debut.

The game will be broadcast live on Netflix, reaching more than 200 countries, while the Jonas Brothers will perform a half-time show.

Who will reach Super Bowl? - NFL predictions for 2026 season

California is 17 hours behind Melbourne and the flight takes about 16 hours. The previous longest for a regular-season game was about 12 hours to Sao Paulo, Brazil.

Yet the two teams have taken a completely different approach. The 49ers arrived in Melbourne last Friday while the Rams arrived the day before the game - just as they did for last year's comfortable win at Wembley over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The huge time difference means that the game kicks off at 10:35 on Friday in Melbourne - which is Thursday evening in the United States: 17:35 on the west coast, 20:35 on the east.

While a morning start (local time) is virtually unheard of in the NFL, it's perfectly normal for fans used to watching cricket at the MCG.

The long flights and early start have thrown each teams' regular routine out of kilter. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan admitted he was struggling to remember what day it was.

But having the game in week one gives each team the best chance to cope with the travel demands, rather than playing it later in the season.

Kelce's last dance? Five things to look out for in new NFL season

The NFL has committed to playing one more game in Melbourne in the next three years, with the possibility of another.

What sets Australia apart from other countries hosting international games is that ball-carrying sports are the most popular down under.

All seven Australians in the NFL converted from rugby, basketball or Australian rules football, and Australia has a huge pool of similar athletes with transferable skills.

The NFL has pledged to provide flag football kits to every school in Australia and opened an academy on the Gold Coast as it aims to tap into that talent, which could produce an international pipeline of players targeting the Olympics and the NFL.

title: John Cominsky details NFL retirement, new project with HOF honors next
description: Ex-Detroit Lions defensive lineman John Cominsky will be inducted into the Summit County Sports Hall of Fame and the Barberton Sports HOF this fall.
fullText:
John Cominsky has redirected the energy he needed to ascend from an underdog at Barberton High School to a starter on an NFL playoff team, using his commitment and passion to promote health education after retiring as a defensive lineman in March 2025.

Cominsky recently told the Beacon Journal he suffered "three significant" concussions as a member of the Detroit Lions in 2023. Those injuries contributed to him leaving the NFL and shifting more of his attention to assisting communities in Northeast Ohio through his Cominsky Family Foundation.

For the past six months, Cominsky has been making weekly visits to a drug and alcohol treatment center in Massillon, where he works with patients on breathing techniques and light exercise.

"It empowers an individual to see, 'Hey, if I move and breathe, I can flush this thought, I can get back to center, I can start my day off right and I can change my attitude,'" said Cominsky, who lives in Hinckley.

Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year

In the meantime, Cominsky's supporters are honoring him for his on-field achievements. He will be inducted into the Summit County Sports Hall of Fame on Oct. 6 and the Barberton Sports Hall of Fame on Nov. 25.

The 30-year-old Cominsky said he's eager to celebrate his fellow inductees and express gratitude to his backers.

"I'm just proud to represent all those people that invested in me," he said.

More local sports: Summit County Sports Hall of Fame's new class has Akron Zips greats and former NFL players

Cominsky transformed from a lightly recruited jack-of-all-trades Barberton football player who quarterbacked the Magics as a senior to a 285-pound defensive end at Division II University of Charleston in West Virginia.

Eating became a job for Cominsky in college as he gained about 70 pounds and evolved into a dominant force in the trenches. He earned All-America status and the Mountain East Conference Defensive Player of the Year award en route to becoming the first Charleston player to be drafted in 68 years when the Atlanta Falcons chose him in the fourth round (No. 135 overall) in 2019.

Cominsky played five seasons in the NFL (three with the Falcons and two with the Lions) and started 20 of the 57 regular-season games in which he appeared, compiling 107 tackles, with 11 for loss and 7.5 sacks, 25 quarterback hits, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery and six passes defensed. In Cominsky's final season, he started 11 of 17 regular-season games and all three playoff games for the 2023 Lions while they made a run to the NFC championship game.

As a member of the Summit County Sports Hall of Fame's board of directors and the president of the Barberton Sports Hall of Fame, Rob Culbertson championed Cominsky's candidacy for his upcoming inductions. Culbertson was a teacher, athletic trainer and athletic director at Barberton during Cominsky's high school years.

"It is just mind-boggling that he was able to take his body and his mind and set a course for himself, set goals, and then he worked his tail off, did as his coaches told him to do, gained the weight and, lo and behold, he was able to get drafted," Culbertson said. "… He is the epitome of what the Barberton community is all about."

Cominsky hasn't forgotten his roots. He and his wife, Brittany, a fellow Barberton native, run the Cominsky Family Foundation. They have held a free youth football camp at Barberton High School for years, aided local businesses, given kids backpacks filled with non-perishable food items and delivered turkeys to pantries for Thanksgiving.

"We also are working with other organizations trying to bolster the out-of-school-time youth experience in Barberton year-round," John Cominsky said.

More John Cominsky: 'It's once in a lifetime': Barberton native helps 2023 Lions reach NFC title game

Meanwhile, health education is at the forefront of Cominsky's plans. A separate business venture in Massillon made him aware of the OVP Health Recovery Center, the drug and alcohol treatment facility where he encourages patients to breathe and move.

Cominsky calls the sessions he hosts "teatime." As an icebreaker of sorts, he wheels in a cart with hot water, tea bags and honey, offering beverages to patients who may be guarded.

"The tea is just this warm welcome," Cominsky said.

The meetings typically last for a half hour to an hour.

"I believe in meditation. I believe in breathing techniques," Cominsky said. "But when you come in with that as your spearhead, people will reject you.

"I go in and we just do basic movement and breath work. I introduce myself, 'Hey, I'm John. I believe moving and breathing is good for you. Who wants to join me?'

"It gives these people an opportunity to see the power of simple habits and routine and just how much discipline, although people see it as restricting freedom, it actually creates freedom."

About 15 to 20 people attend "teatime" each week in Massillon, Cominsky said. He has also dabbled in events with IBF Addiction Recovery in Akron.

"I've kind of wiggled my way into drug recovery without being a former addict myself, which is pretty unlikely," Cominsky said. "Even the higher-up leaders [at rehabilitation centers], a lot of them have fought addiction themselves, and so I feel grateful to have the conviction to serve this community without the history."

Cominsky said he has a desire for people to be healthy, and he wants them to prioritize health. He thought about becoming a doctor — or a pursuing another profession in the medical field — as a biology and chemistry major at Charleston. He said his enthusiasm for health and wellness would exist even if his football career had not ended the way it did, with concerns about the concussions he has endured.

"But it shines a little bit more light on it because I kind of have these lingering issues," Cominsky said. "In boxing, they call it punch-drunk. It's kind of like you have half a beer in you all the time. It's kind of like a slight vertigo. It's something I've grown used to, and it has improved.

"I have a true a gauge [for inflammation in my body] because my symptoms flare up. It's directly related to poor habits. It's directly related to if I have bad sleep, if I eat bad, if I'm dehydrated. All these things flare up."

Cominsky also suffered a torn medial collateral ligament and cartilage damage in his right knee early in the Lions' 2024 training camp. He underwent surgery and never played again in the NFL.

"I had a lot of cartilage that kind of got chipped out," he said, "almost like a golf divot right under my kneecap, and that's what was giving me most of the issues.

"I'm still dealing with things in my knee. I have a lot of cartilage missing, and it really took a while to bounce back, probably a full two years after the injury to feel 90%."

Cominsky said a silver lining is the knee injury "probably saved my brain a little bit" by sidelining him for the entire 2024 season.

As Cominsky reflected on his NFL career in 2024, he concluded the concussions from the previous year had affected his performance on the field.

"I'm looking at my game film, and I'm just watching a little bit of hesitancy," Cominsky said. "My edge when I played was that I played with my hair on fire, and I had no remorse for anything, anybody, my own body, whatever.

"I started to see myself make what they call in the NFL 'business decisions.' There's a play. The guy's probably going to go down. Just peel away. You don't have to stick your nose in there. So, I started to see these signs of like, 'Oh, buddy. Hey, you're losing your edge a little bit.'"

Of course, Cominsky thought about his future with his family, too. In 2022, he and Brittany had their first child, now 4-year-old daughter Emersyn. In 2024, Brittany became pregnant with the couple's now 1-year-old son, Wren.

"Between my family developing and the concussions that I had, I just didn't have the fire that was required of me," Cominsky said. "… I just couldn't do it, and so I was very fortunate to be able to walk away.

"It was just too many concussions, and I lost my fire. There's guys out there with fire times a hundred, and you don't want to be on the same field as somebody who is all in when you're not 100% in. So, it was time."

Cominsky turned to a new chapter, and he plans to write many more.

"I'm pretty set on this health education piece and bringing that to all people, including vulnerable populations," he said.

title: ‘When You Drinking, Nothing Really Good Comes From It’ — Pro Bowler Reacts to Mark Sanchez’s Guilty Plea Plan in Stabbing Incident
description: Mark Sanchez’s legal saga took a significant turn last week when the former NFL quarterback and ex-Fox Sports analyst filed a motion to plead guilty to charges stemming from an October 2025 altercation with a truck driver in Indianapolis. Sanchez faced a felony battery charge and three misdemeanors, including public intoxication and unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, after the alcohol-fueled confrontation left both him and 69-year-old Perry Tole seriously injured.
fullText:
Mark Sanchez's legal saga took a significant turn last week when the former NFL quarterback and ex-Fox Sports analyst filed a motion to plead guilty to charges stemming from an October 2025 altercation with a truck driver in Indianapolis.

Sanchez faced a felony battery charge and three misdemeanors, including public intoxication and unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, after the alcohol-fueled confrontation left both him and 69-year-old Perry Tole seriously injured.

The guilty plea came just five days before his jury trial was set to begin, and former Pro Bowl wide receiver T.J. Houshmandzadeh, who has known Sanchez since he was a teenager, shared his reaction to the news.

Sanchez had been in Indianapolis to call the Raiders-Colts game for Fox on Oct. 5, 2025, when, in the early morning hours of Oct. 4, prosecutors say he accosted Tole in an alley between two downtown hotels while the truck driver was collecting used cooking oil.

The encounter escalated as Tole stabbed Sanchez in self-defense and was not charged, and both men were hospitalized. Fox Sports fired Sanchez in November and replaced him with Drew Brees.

The guilty plea, filed in Marion County Superior Court, requested that the judge vacate the Sept. 8 trial date and schedule a sentencing hearing. It remains unclear which specific charges Sanchez is pleading guilty to, and a judge still needs to formally accept the plea.

Houshmandzadeh, a former Cincinnati Bengals wideout who made the Pro Bowl in 2007, expressed sympathy for Sanchez while acknowledging alcohol's role in the incident.

"It's just unfortunate," Houshmandzadeh said. "It was an unfortunate situation for Mark because I've known Mark since he was a teenager… Great person. So when I saw this, I was like, 'Mark Sanchez did this?' It shocked me. And so, when you drinking, I guess nothing really good comes from it. And so the good thing is Mark is okay. The gentleman that he 'assaulted' is okay. At least I believe he's okay."

Houshmandzadeh also offered his take on the logic behind pleading guilty when the evidence is difficult to dispute.

"If it's on video, what am I pleading not guilty for?" he added. "You see it clear as day. You see pictures of the injuries, and so you don't want to have to relive that moment. Neither one of those guys want to have to relive that moment. Now, what does that entail, though, by me pleading guilty, what does that entail?"

"I got probation? Do I get community service?" Houshmandzadeh continued. "Because if it entails that I got to go to jail, and I've never really been in jail, oh, I'm not pleading guilty. I'm going to go ahead and press my luck. So, I would assume it's just going to be some probation, some things he's going to have to do community service-wise, and he'll do that no problem."

The plea deal appears to be part of a broader effort to resolve both the criminal and civil cases simultaneously. Tole has a pending civil lawsuit against Sanchez and Fox Sports, and his attorney Matt Golitko said the two sides are on "a positive path toward an agreement."

NFL insider Mike Florio noted recently that in cases like these, a civil settlement often shapes the criminal outcome, explaining that when a victim is "placated by, for example, a sizable settlement of the civil case," prosecutors are more likely to allow a plea that doesn't involve jail time.

Fox Sports has moved on with Brees in the analyst role alongside play-by-play voice Adam Amin, but the broadcasting world hasn't entirely closed its doors on Sanchez.

If the criminal case ends with probation and community service, and the civil suit reaches an amicable resolution, a return to television isn't out of the question. It won't be at Fox, at least not anytime soon, but Sanchez's decade of NFL experience and three years in the broadcasting booth give him a foundation to rebuild from once the off-field issues are put to rest.

title: Christian Gonzalez addresses trainer’s contract negotiation comments
description: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez reacts to the public contract comments made by his trainer on sports radio.
fullText:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. – Christian Gonzalez has stayed fairly quiet regarding his ongoing contract negotiations with the New England Patriots. However, his trainer did quite the opposite.

Christian White recently went on 98.5 The Sports Hub's "Felger and Mazz" to discuss the contract negotiations, saying that while he thought that they were "getting close," the language in the Patriots' offer was "kind of trash."

"It was true at the time, but it's just not all the way true," White said in regard to Kraft's comments about the organization willing to make him the highest-paid cornerback. "Like, the context is like, yeah we did offer you to be the highest paid, but contract language was kind of trash. So, we kind of had to sort through that stuff to make it make sense."

"He's expressed to everybody, he wants to be there," he added. "He's fell in love with the place. He wants to be there for however many more years they agree on the extension, and probably even further after that. I'm just hoping they do right by him."

And with that, White made a bold prediction, saying that he "wouldn't be shocked if this gets done before the Seattle game."

So, what did Gonzalez think of White's comments? Was he upset about his trainer speaking out publicly when he's made a point of keeping it out of the media?

"That's my guy. We have two different opinions," Gonzalez said. "I mean, he's a grown man. If he wants to go talk on the media, he's gonna go talk on the media. He's my guy. I trust him with everything. He trusts me with everything. We talk every day. So it wasn't anything to me that was bad, or I mean, he went and talked to them. So, I talked to him maybe two hours after I came back and saw all that. So I mean, nothing crazy at all.

"We joked about other things, but not about what he said."

title: Badiashile suffers nightmare Napoli debut as Chelsea loanee slammed: ‘His fault’

fullText:
Chelsea loanee Benoît Badiashile received low ratings from Italian sports papers following Napoli's 3-2 loss against Inter, with the French centre-back blamed for two of the Nerazzurri's goals.

Napoli wasted a two-goal lead in their away game against Inter on Saturday, suffering their second consecutive loss in Serie A.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Marcus Thuram of Internazionale celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Chelsea loanee Badiashile made his Serie A debut coming off the bench in the final ten minutes, with the Partenopei leading 2-1, but his impact was beyond negative.

Inter striker Thuram overjumped him to score Inter's equaliser, but the Napoli defender was also blamed for the Nerazzurri's winner, scored by Lautaro Martinez in stoppage time.

Football Italia rated Badiashile 5/10, the same mark he received from Gazzetta dello Sport and Tuttosport.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli, reacts during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Gazzetta blamed Badiashile for Inter's second goal, but also criticised Massimiliano Allegri for introducing the Chelsea loanee: "Badiashile lost Thuram, who headed home the equaliser," the pink paper wrote.

"It was his fault, but also the fault of whoever decided to bring on a new defender who hadn't played in ages at the most crucial moment."

Corriere dello Sport was even harsher on Badiashile, rating him 4.5/10: "He hadn't played since March 7, and he showed. Thuram outjumped him for the header, and he was also partly at fault for the third goal."

LONDON, ENGLAND – JANUARY 31: Benoit Badiashile of Chelsea reacts during the Premier League match between Chelsea and West Ham United at Stamford Bridge on January 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Badiashile joined Napoli on a paid €3m loan deal from Chelsea this summer. The Partenopei have an option to make his move permanent for €27m at the end of the season.

Napoli's next game is against Arsenal at the Stadio Maradona next Wednesday, in their 2026-27 Champions League opener.

title: How bullying led Britain's Campbell to the UFC
description: Introduced to combat sports as a seven-year-old after being bullied at school, Kurtis Campbell is now chasing success in the UFC.
fullText:
Kurtis Campbell was only seven years old when his parents decided something drastically needed to change.

During his time at primary school in Liverpool, Campbell was targeted by bullies. His parents, Jay and Michelle, could see the effect it was having.

It was then that they signed him up for Muay Thai classes to help him learn how to defend himself.

"From there, I've never looked back," Briton Campbell told BBC Sport. "I've been in love with the sport ever since."

Without his parents' influence and support, the 24-year-old would not be chasing his dream of becoming a UFC champion.

Seventeen years later Campbell is preparing for his second fight in the promotion against American Trevor Peek at UFC Paris on Saturday.

"I'm not going to stop until my mum and dad are on a beach somewhere, sipping cocktails and doing nothing else for the rest of their lives," Campbell said.

"They can enjoy it, knowing that they've created this monster. That's my plan."

Initially, it seemed Campbell's time in the gym would serve the sole purpose of learning self-defence before moving to secondary school a couple of years later.

That was until he started competing in amateur competitions, slowly but surely becoming obsessed with his newfound escape from the difficulties he faced at school.

"I was quite a soft kid, in the sense that I didn't really like the violence or the fighting," Campbell said.

"I felt like when I did fight, and when I really did go into it, everything changed and I never looked back."

Aged 15, he won his first international Muay Thai title and started to realise that, with the blessing of his parents, combat sports could become more than just a pastime.

"I was never the cleverest kid. I was always in the bottom sets at school, so I wasn't really focused," Campbell said.

"All of the teachers told me, 'you need to do something else. You have to have a plan B.'"

But for Campbell, who was beginning to attract attention across Merseyside, his unwavering commitment to the sport meant there was no need for a back-up plan.

That included regularly running almost five miles to and from school. There was even one occasion when he missed school while studying for his GCSEs to attend a coaching seminar in Liverpool hosted by John Kavanagh - the coach of former two-weight UFC champion Conor McGregor.

After completing his GCSE exams at the age of 16, Campbell enrolled on a college course that combined studying for a qualification in sport with playing football.

Or at least that was what he was supposed to be doing.

Campbell struck an arrangement with the course leads that allowed him to attend classes before leaving to train in combat sports, while his peers were on the football pitch.

"I was always avoiding anything just for fighting," Campbell said.

"I really didn't like school. It wasn't me. But I made a good few mates there, so you've got to take the pros with the cons."

When Campbell suffered a TKO defeat by Danny Silva on his UFC debut in March, it was the first time in almost seven and a half years that he had lost.

Not since December 2018, when he lost to fellow Liverpudlian Liam McCracken on the local amateur circuit, had featherweight Campbell failed to get his hand raised.

He won five titles across three different weight classes with the Full Contact Contender (FCC) promotion before earning a UFC contract on Dana White's Contender Series in September 2025.

It means that when he steps into the Accor Arena to fight Peek, he will face the unfamiliar feeling of trying to bounce back from defeat.

"Fighting in the UFC was just the goal and the dream when I was younger," Campbell said.

"So I feel like that fat kid looking back at me would be proud of me. I would be proud of myself, no matter how the debut went, just because of where I am now.

"I think he'd be happy with me. But I know he'd not be happy with just the story. I've still got a lot of legacy to build.

"That's one thing I would say is good and bad about me - as soon as I get something, I want more of it.

"I don't think I'll ever stop having that feeling."

title: No away fans for Old Firm games this season after agreement reached
description: There will be no away supporters for Celtic and Rangers derbies in the Scottish Premiership or Premier Sports Cup this season.
fullText:
There will be no away supporters for Celtic and Rangers derbies in the Scottish Premiership or Premier Sports Cup this season.

The "temporary arrangement" was reached following talks between the Glasgow clubs and the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL).

It follows the Scottish FA's independent review into events surrounding last term's Scottish Cup quarter-final at Ibrox, which was marred by unrest and pitch incursions from both sets of fans.

Rangers host Celtic in the Premier Sports Cup on 13 September, with the city rivals meeting at Celtic Park in the league a week later.

Rangers had proposed a reduced away allocation of 300 for the impending cup tie, with Celtic rejecting the offer.

The crowd disorder on 8 March came after a penalty shootout win for Celtic, when around 8,000 visiting supporters had been present.

That figure was much larger than recent Old Firm league derbies, with ticketing rules different for the Scottish Cup.

The Scottish FA announced last month that both clubs would have to play their next Scottish Cup home games behind closed doors.

Announcing the measures, a statement from the SPFL said: "This temporary arrangement will allow both clubs, together with the SPFL, Police Scotland and other relevant stakeholders, to give proper consideration to the findings and recommendations of the independent review, take forward the necessary actions and ensure sufficient time is available to plan future fixtures thoroughly.

"It will also provide greater certainty for supporters and those involved in matchday planning, while avoiding repeated uncertainty around ticketing arrangements for individual fixtures.

"All parties have committed to working constructively during this period, with safety and security remaining the priority."

The March cup meeting was the first time Celtic supporters have been given the full Broomloan Road Stand allocation at Ibrox since away allocations were reduced to fewer than 1,000 in 2018.

The number of away fans at both Ibrox and Celtic Park fluctuated between about 800 and zero in a series of tit-for-tat moves before an arrangement was reached for "around 5%" capacity [2,500 - 3,000] for league games in 2025 and 2026.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes described the news as "disappointing", saying: "It's always better when opposition fans are allowed into a derby game.

"In the context of everything that's gone on with this fixture and the last part of it, I think there's a lot to consider and a lot to discuss.

"As far as I was led to believe, that was still up for discussion, so it's kind of caught me on the hop a wee bit."

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill described the decision as "inevitable" and "really sad".

O'Neill added: "It's a great, great fixture when the ground is absolutely full. And I think the away fans make this.

"Hopefully the two clubs will maybe get together at some stage or another and try to iron out the particular problems."

title: Trio of Iowa football legends named to USA TODAY's all-2000s team

Kaeding is Iowa's career scoring leader with 373 points. The 2002 recipient of the Lou Groza Award, Kaeding was also a consensus All-American following his standout 2003 season. title: Astros' AL West dominance may face a $4 billion threat in Southern California
description: The Astros' longtime divisional punching bag just gained one of the richest and most accomplished owners in sports.
fullText:
The Houston Astros have essentially owned the American League West for a decade now, winning seven division titles, four American League pennants and two World Series championships. However, the Astros' divisional dominance could be up for grabs, as the organization must manage an aging roster and a likely need for new leadership in multiple positions.

On Tuesday, a new threat entered the proverbial AL West chat, with a resume that features a championship-winning pedigree across every major sport on two continents.

Billionaire team owner Stan Kroenke and Kroenke Sports Entertainment (KSE) entered into a definitive agreement on Tuesday to purchase the Los Angeles Angels from the Arte Moreno family for a reported MLB-record $4 billion. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027.

"The Angels are a storied franchise anchored in a great market," Kroenke said in a statement released by both the Angels and Kroenke Sports & Entertainment. "We look forward to an exciting future with the Angels organization."

Kroenke, who owns four franchises across four leagues, will likely bring a fresh perspective to a franchise that's been moribund and listless. The Angels are on track to miss the postseason for the 12th straight year and have essentially wasted the prime years of two of the best baseball talents of a generation in Shohei Ohtani and Mike Trout.

Under Kroenke's leadership, his teams have all won titles in the past five years, including:

English Premier League's Arsenal, 2026

A championship standard is now attainable KSE's as foundation for success, not just an aspirational one. Josh Kroenke, Arsenal's co-chairman, demonstrated these aspirations when hiring Andrea Berta as the club's new sporting director.

"I went to Andrea, and I laid out our championship rings," Josh Kroenke said to James Benge of CBS in May. "I said: 'This is what we're here for. So as we start to shape our thinking, know this is what we're going for.' He was looking at them pretty close!"

KSE isn't simply purchasing a baseball team; they're buying back into Southern California in an area that's highly valuable yet wholly undeveloped in Orange County. Kroenke's institutional knowledge means there is a real possibility of turning an aging ballpark and sports district into another year-round real estate and entertainment engine.

"The addition of the Angels to the KSE portfolio creates the opportunity for a year-round Southern California calendar of events," reads a statement from KSE on their future strategy.

The Angels sit on land-currently owned by the City of Anaheim-that could ultimately be more valuable than the team itself. Angel Stadium sits on approximately 150 acres, with surrounding areas potentially up for grabs. In fact, KSE recently developed SoFi Stadium as the anchor of a 300-acre Hollywood Park entertainment district focused on retail, offices, residences and hotels.

The Angels' reputation has suffered greatly under previous ownership, as the squandering of talents like Ohtani and Moreno has coincided with reports of downsizing in scouting, development and organizational resources. KSE's ownership has continually focused on stadium upgrades, revamped clubhouses, sports science investment and family-friendly facilities for players.

That type of resource commitment is enough to attract marquee players to any organization, but offering a Southern California lifestyle that includes year-round good weather, access to beaches, major entertainment opportunities, and increased endorsement potential can be a big joker in negotiations.

"Kroenke's got a track record of success and winning championships with his teams," Trout said to reporters on Tuesday. "I'm super excited about it and can't wait to meet him."

Just ask the Los Angeles Dodgers about offering such a benefit to free agents.

The Astros already booted their general manager in August, and Joe Espada's tenure as manager is clearly in doubt. Moreover, Astros owner Jim Crane has already shown hesitancy to spend big, instead relying on a cautious, methodical approach.

That strategy served the Astros well during their title-winning run, as their roster was stacked with future Hall of Famers and a minor league system stocked with future All-Stars. The club also featured rising stars in various leadership positions that proved to be innovative (and at times, too clever) before moving on to other teams. Playing in a warm-weather city with lucrative tax benefits has always been a plus, but for some, playing in Southern California has an appeal all its own.

The AL West includes teams that are either resource-rich but inconsistent, like the Seattle Mariners and Texas Rangers, or struggling significantly, such as the Athletics and Angels. In this environment, being consistently competent has been key to success, as the Astros have demonstrated for over a decade. But 2026 has proven how low the bar is for competency.

"The reality is no AL West team really deserves to reach the postseason this year. All five teams deserve to go home at the end of September," Yahoo MLB insider Russell Dorsey said in August. "But it doesn't work that way in baseball. So we all have to resign ourselves to watching maybe the saddest division race MLB has ever seen."

The Astros have a 138-89 record against the Angels since joining the AL West in 2013, but competency has now landed in Southern California. The Astros should prepare themselves accordingly.

title: Angels’ Outfield Depth in Trouble After Josh Lowe Injury Scratch
description: The Los Angeles Angels scratched outfielder Josh Lowe from Wednesday's game against the New York Yankees with neck stiffness. The post Angels’ Outfield Depth in Trouble After Josh Lowe Injury Scratch appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Angels scratched outfielder Josh Lowe from Wednesday's game against the New York Yankees with neck stiffness.

The Angels' outfield is severely lacking in depth, as they currently have just four outfielders listed on their active roster—one of whom is Lowe. Wade Meckler will move over to right field to cover for Lowe, with Jose Siri getting the start in left field.

Lowe, an offseason acquisition from the Tampa Bay Rays, has been with the Angels for nearly the entire season, only being away from the team during a month-long stint in Triple-A. He can play any position across the outfield, providing valuable depth in each position for the Halos.

The 28-year-old has 10 homers on the year, driving in 27 runs through 95 games this season. He has a .625 OPS this season, which would be the lowest mark of his career if he finishes the season at this pace.

His best stretch of baseball came after the Angels recalled him from Triple-A in June, where he went 8-for-18 through his final six games of June. He hit a homer and drove in four runs during that stretch, posting an OPS north of 1.000 during his hot streak.

Siri, Meckler and Mike Trout are the only other players explicitly listed as outfielders on the Angels' roster, though they have other players who could stand in if needed.

Other than Lowe, Siri, Meckler and Trout, the Angels have a few options if they need to bring someone into the outfield later in the year.

Kyren Paris came up from Triple-A Tuesday for the Angels' September call-ups, and he has plenty of experience in the outfield despite primarily playing in the middle of the infield. 2024 first-round pick Christian Moore also primarily plays in the infield, but the Angels tested him out in left field when they called him up earlier in the season.

Lastly, Adam Frazier has spent some time in the outfield this season for the Angels, and could fill in if needed.

Even still, the Angels' outfield is running extremely thin, and remains an area they'll have to reinforce come the offseason.

title: Tom Brady's sports memorabilia store to open in downtown Indianapolis
description: CardVault by Tom Brady will open at a central downtown corner this fall, bringing the former quarterback's brand to Indiana.
fullText:
Tom Brady will be setting up shop in Indianapolis. No, not on the football team.

CardVault by Tom Brady, a sports and trading cards, collectibles and memorabilia shop co-founded by the former Patriots quarterback, will open at 2 W. Washington St. in downtown Indianapolis later this year, said Nick Wright, who leases retail spaces on the building's ground floor.

The company signed a 10-year lease in the building known as the H.P. Wasson & Company Building.

CardVault leadership wants to open the Indianapolis store as soon as possible, Wright said. The initial plans called for opening by the first Colts home game, slated for Sunday, Sept. 13, but that's not likely to happen.

Wright deferred IndyStar to CardVault for more specific information on the grand opening, which Wright said Brady will likely attend. IndyStar's attempts to contact CardVault before publication were unsuccessful.

CardVault was established during the pandemic in 2020. Since then, the brand has become one of the fastest growing collectibles retail stores in the country, opening in "major cities near iconic venues," according to CardVault's website.

Currently, CardVault operates 17 brick-and-mortar stores alongside a handful of vending machine operations in Los Angeles, Boston and Minneapolis, where it sells sports memorabilia and trading cards brands, such as Pokémon. Inside, collectors can also submit items for grading.

CardVault's rise builds on a booming, multi-billion-dollar collectibles industry that has brought increased attention to the hobby of sports and trading cards. The industry is projected to be worth nearly $7 billion by 2035.

The store's spot in Indianapolis taps into the dedicated sports community, the annual presence of Gen Con at the convention center and regional sports shows, like the National Sports Collectors Convention held in Chicago earlier this summer.

Across the country, CardVault has been experimenting with setting up shop in downtown areas.

"It'll be a great place for people to get together and trade," Wright said of the Indianapolis store. "I'm really, really looking forward to seeing collectors, sports fans, visitors come together in this space. It's good for downtown and the growing collectibles industry."

The storefront on the northwest corner of the Meridian and Washington streets intersection has not been available for nearly two decades, Wright said. T-Mobile moved out of the space earlier this month. When the company moved out, Wright wanted to veer away from the typical coffee shop or restaurant space, aiming to bring an "experiential" store to the high-trafficked and visible corner.

Wright described CardVault as a win-win for downtown retail and the collectibles industry in Indianapolis.

"It says a lot about Indianapolis," Wright said.

title: Charlie Baker: When NFL, NBA players return to campus, everyone else pays the price
description: All four Power Conferences have signed off on the Protect College Sports Act. NCAA President Charlie Baker writes why it must be passed into law.
fullText:
The notion college sports are for college students who will move on when they complete their degree or turn pro enjoys near-universal support. But right now, that fundamental boundary is being dismantled amid a relentless wave of litigation.

In two cases, the NCAA has been ordered to allow professional basketball players to return to college basketball, despite the fact they intentionally left college to go to the NBA Draft and each played in several NBA games. In another case, a judge required the NCAA to allow an athlete to compete for a fifth school in five years. And in the past two weeks, without so much as a hearing, let alone a trial, two courts permitted NFL players to return immediately to college football. These few examples are merely the tip of the iceberg.

POWER PLAY: College football's 25 most powerful people

OP-ED: Federal antitrust protection is only workable path to saving college sports

Eligibility rules have long held a simple purpose: Ensuring a fair playing field while preserving access to the life-changing benefits college sports provide to actual college students. For decades, that standard meant allowing student-athletes four seasons of competition over five years. Recognizing the need for evolution, NCAA member schools recently updated this rule to allow up to five years of competition before age 24. However, since the start of 2025, more than 165 lawsuits have been filed seeking to tear down these basic limits.

As rosters are increasingly packed with older adults and former professionals, the most obvious consequence is an unfair matchup on the field. But the longer-term impact falls on the next generation of young athletes who will be squeezed out of the system as a result. Sidelining incoming freshmen doesn't just rob them of their roster spots or athletic scholarship opportunities — it also strips away their chance to experience the lifelong benefits of college sports. In addition, adding former professionals to rosters costs already-enrolled student-athletes valuable playing time and development opportunities during their precious years in college.

Amid this chaos, the need to pass the Protect College Sports Act is more apparent than ever. This bipartisan bill addresses the current legal instability head-on by creating one clear, fair and enforceable eligibility standard to prevent further erosion of the competitive balance that makes college sports meaningful. Crucially, the PCSA does not stop there. It also codifies important student-athlete benefits into law, including scholarship, healthcare and revenue-sharing protections. And it takes steps to protect broad opportunities, particularly in women's and Olympic sports, by establishing sport minimums and roster protections.

This balanced approach has earned the PCSA a broad consensus of support, uniting professional, Olympic and collegiate sport groups — including student-athlete leaders and conferences across all three divisions — all of whom recognize what's at stake right now for the future of college athletics.

As the Senate prepares to return from recess and the new school year begins, the urgency is higher than ever. College sports matter. They serve our nation's youth, and I believe they are the greatest human development tool in the entire world. By passing the PCSA, lawmakers can ensure they continue to benefit young generations of athletes for decades to come.

Charlie Baker is president of the NCAA.

title: ‘The league’s a disaster right now’: Mike Francesa calls out WNBA
description: It’s been a wild summer for the WNBA, between the seemingly endless controversies involving Caitlin Clark and all of the political firestorm that ensued after Sophie Cunningham spoke out against transgender women in women’s sports. While it’s certainly led to a lot of media attention, it isn’t exactly good attention. Over the past few months,…
fullText:
It's been a wild summer for the WNBA, between the seemingly endless controversies involving Caitlin Clark and all of the political firestorm that ensued after Sophie Cunningham spoke out against transgender women in women's sports. While it's certainly led to a lot of media attention, it isn't exactly good attention.

Over the past few months, the WNBA has become the most toxic space in all sports as players and the league itself have become political pawns. Now, longtime radio host Mike Francesa is calling out the league's leadership.

During his podcast this week, Mike Francesa was asked his take on the current state of the WNBA, and he was certainly not shy about blaming the WNBA's leadership for not having the foresight to see how things would change once Clark entered the league and the players for not welcoming her.

"They have turned their league into a bubbling, volcanic, political, chaotic situation where every nut is now getting involved politically in the WNBA on all different levels," Francesa ranted on his podcast. "It's the worst thing that could have ever happened. I blame the people who run the league, I blame the players who didn't have the long-range vision and didn't have the smarts to realize what Caitlin Clark was going to do for their league, and instead, tried to hurt her and run her out of the league at every point."

Francesa went on to compare Clark to when Pete Maravich joined the Atlanta Hawks.

"There were revolts against Pete Maravich when he came to the NBA," Francesa recalled. "He broke up a very good Atlanta Hawks team because there was insane jealousy and people felt he hadn't earned anything and they felt he was just a self-promoting showboat."

While the issues might have started with Clark, Francesa acknowledges that the issues are far beyond her at this point.

"Caitlin Clark came to that league and energized it in a way that they had never seen possible," Francesa added.  "They had never been able to sell that league to anybody, and she sold it to everybody. And they're all trying to ruin it. And now it's become a political mess way past just the issues with Caitlin Clark. The league's a disaster right now."

title: Family sues after 6-year-old girl dies when badminton racket shaft pierces skull
description: A New Jersey family's wrongful death lawsuit alleges Franklin Sports sold a defective badminton racket that fatally struck 6-year-old Lucy Morgan in Maine.
fullText:
The family of a 6-year-old New Jersey girl who died after a badminton racket came apart and pierced her skull during a Maine vacation is suing the Massachusetts-based maker of the sports equipment.

"This case represents a parent's worst nightmare," attorney Charles P. Hehmeyer, who is representing the family, said. "The Morgan family was enjoying an idyllic summer vacation here in Maine when they lost Lucy due to what we allege was a dangerous and defective piece of sports equipment."

The wrongful death and product-liability lawsuit alleges Franklin Sports sold a defective and unreasonably dangerous badminton racket that failed during normal use and turned its metal shaft into a projectile.

Lucy Morgan was vacationing with her parents and siblings in Limerick, Maine, on June 1, 2024, when the tragedy unfolded.

College Grad Reportedly Dies In Six Flags Roller Coaster Incident As Family Sues Theme Park

Maine State Police said Lucy's 10-year-old brother was playing outside when the aluminum shaft became dislodged from the wooden handle. The shaft struck Lucy in the head and pierced her skull, authorities said.

Lucy was taken to Southern Maine Health Care in Sanford before being airlifted to Maine Medical Center in Portland, where she died June 5, 2024, police said.

U.s. Track Star Sues Puma Team Over F1 Team-designed Gear She Says Caused Career-ending Injury

According to a copy of the complaint obtained by Fox News Digital, the Franklin badminton set had been supplied at the family's rental cottage.

The lawsuit alleges the racket's handle and metal shaft were not adequately secured, the adhesive joining the pieces was defective or insufficient, and the design lacked a secondary restraint that could have prevented the metal portion from flying free. The family also alleges Franklin Sports failed to warn consumers about the risk.

Hehmeyer told WCVB 5 that the case was not Franklin Sports' first issue involving a racket separating. He said a child in New York lost an eye when a racket came apart, and alleged the company knew of that case but failed to make a fix.

Montana Boy Killed After Being Flung From Carnival Ride Operating With Missing Restraints, Lawsuit Alleges

"The company knew that but chose not to correct this with something as simple as a pin in the handle, which would cost pennies," Hehmeyer told the outlet.

The lawsuit seeks compensatory and punitive damages, though it does not list a specific dollar figure. The family is seeking funeral expenses, emotional distress damages, loss of comfort, society and companionship, and other relief permitted under Maine law.

According to the complaint, Lucy's three siblings witnessed the incident and suffered "severe emotional distress." Her parents heard her screaming and ran to her aid, the complaint alleges.

Heartbroken Fathers Find Divine Hope In Secret Notes Left By Girls Killed In Camp Mystic Flood

Lucy's father, Jesse Morgan, a pastor at Green Pond Bible Chapel in Rockaway, New Jersey, previously wrote that the family had been spending its final full day at a lake cottage when the children decided to play badminton in the front yard.

Florida 3-Year-old Dies After Tragic Incident Involving Common Play Toy At Babysitter's House

In the days following Lucy's death, Jesse Morgan shared the faith that sustained his family through their grief. He told Fox News Digital that a friend returned Lucy's backpack after the family came home from Maine, and inside was the prayer journal she had received about a month before she died. The journal contained drawings, Bible-themed notes and messages about her belief in God, her father said.

Jesse Morgan told Fox News Digital he had no doubt Lucy "loved Christ and loved God," and that God welcomed her into heaven. He described discovering the journal as one of the "most beautiful gifts" amid the family's loss, adding that he believed his daughter had "the faith of a mustard seed."

Franklin Sports told Fox News Digital it "extends its deepest sympathies to Lucy Morgan's family and all those affected by this tragic accident."

"Because litigation is pending, we cannot comment on the specific allegations in the lawsuit," the company said. Franklin Sports added that it takes product-safety concerns "very seriously," is committed to product quality and safety, and is reviewing the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Fox News Digital reached out to attorneys for the Morgan family for comment.

Fox News Digital's Sarah Rumpf-Whitten contributed to this report.

title: Detroit Lions may face one obstacle in any Christian Gonzalez trade pursuit
description: Detroit’s defense intercepted 13 passes last season, tied for 11th in the NFL. Four of those came from cornerbacks, and D.J. Reed accounted for two of them. fullText:
Detroit's defense intercepted 13 passes last season, tied for 11th in the NFL. Four of those came from cornerbacks, and D.J. Reed accounted for two of them.

Carter Bahns and Zachary Pereles of CBS Sports named the Lions on Thursday among five potential landing spots for New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, alongside the Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders, New York Giants and Pittsburgh Steelers.

Terrion Arnold, the 24th pick of the 2024 draft, was released by Detroit in June while facing felony charges he has denied, and he agreed to terms with Seattle this month. Reed inherited the No. 1 job, and the group behind him has been shuffled and interrupted by injuries throughout camp.

Tim Twentyman wrote in the club's own training camp position preview in last month that "the Arnold release hurts Detroit's depth at the position," adding it would not surprise him if general manager Brad Holmes added to the spot before the regular season. That went up five weeks before Gonzalez's name entered the conversation, written by someone the team employs.

Detroit ranked 28th in opponent passer rating in the red zone last season at 104.3, allowing 19 passing touchdowns inside its own 20-yard line without intercepting a throw there. Reed's year split around a hamstring strain that cost him six games, and he turns 30 in November.

Gonzalez turned 24 this summer and has two seasons left on his contract. He closed 2025 with three pass breakups and four solo tackles in New England's Super Bowl LX loss to the Seahawks.

The #Lions are listed as a top landing spot for #Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez if he were to be traded Per CBS Sports pic.twitter.com/shw9ae09nF

— NFL Rumors (@nflrums) August 29, 2026

Gonzalez is playing on a rookie deal worth $4.8 million this season that runs through 2027 after New England exercised his fifth-year option in April. Detroit would inherit two years of control and an immediate negotiation, and that negotiation now starts from a number set this month in Seattle, where Devon Witherspoon signed a four-year extension averaging $33 million a season with $101 million in total guarantees and just over $59 million locked in at signing.

The draft compensation would be the cheaper half of the transaction. Bahns and Pereles made that point about the Lions specifically, writing that a long-term deal for Gonzalez would limit Detroit's flexibility at other positions and that the club can carry it only because the money would not take effect until next year.

Robert Kraft said at the start of training camp that New England had offered Gonzalez a deal that would make him the highest-paid cornerback in league history and the highest-paid player in franchise history.

"We love Christian Gonzalez," Kraft said. "We love him as a player, as a person. That's why we've made an offer to him that makes him the highest-paid player ever to play that position in the NFL, and coincidentally, it's the highest contract in the Patriots franchise history,"

Adam Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show during the week that the sides are "obviously not in the same neighborhood right now and haven't been."

Eliot Wolf, the club's executive vice president of player personnel, answered yes this week when asked if New England still intends to reach that figure.

Gonzalez reported to camp on time and practiced in pads, passing up a holdout that would have cost him $45,000 for every day he missed. He returned to full participation this week after a hard fall on Aug. 10 kept him out of both of the Patriots' first two preseason games. Asked about the standoff, he told reporters it was "frustrating, but I'm focused on the season."

His trainer posted, then deleted, a message on Thursday saying New England should trade him. That remains the loudest anyone in Gonzalez's circle has been all summer.

The Patriots reached Super Bowl LX in February and open this season with a quarterback still on a rookie contract, which places them inside the window where a cornerback of Gonzalez's standing is worth more to them than to anyone else.

fullText:
Sophie Cunningham has dominated nationwide headlines for over a month following her comments against trans athletes' eligibility in women's sports.

On Friday night, it was her play on the hardwood that caught basketball fans' attention. In a comfortable, 20-point win over the Connecticut Sun, Cunningham registered a single point off the bench, and fans weren't all too pleased with her performance, to say the least.

The WNBA world was livid as they expected more from a 'Sixth Player of the Year' candidate.

"Sophie Cunningham scored 1 point in 14 minutes for the Fever tonight. Thought I'd share these stats, since she wants us to talk about basketball now," said one user, who has been sharing her stats on X each time she underperforms.

This post alluded toCunningham's comments on August 5, "I'm going to let people just do the speaking for themselves, but for me, I want to get back to basketball. It's always been about basketball."

Another X user, whileroasting her for her 1-point stat line, wrote, "If only this grifter could hit buckets as well as point fingers. She sucks."

One WNBA observer pointed out that merely a day ago, the Fever created multiple posts to campaign for Cunningham to win the 'Sixth Player of the Year' award.

They wrote, "And the Fever has the nerve to create a 6POY for her," which was followed by numerous crying laughing emojis.

Another kept it simple and wrote, "Enes Kanter stats," alluding to the fact that Kanter, who has also been in headlines since his WNBA Draft declaration, was never a star during his 11-year NBA stint.

Last night's game saw the Fever lead by 15 points at the end of the first half. It was never truly close as Indy ran away with the 111-91 win.

So, it wasn't incumbent upon Cunningham to have a double-digit scoring night and shoot her usual, 44%+ blistering percentage from beyond the arc.

title: Penix Closes Gap as Falcons QB Race Boils Over
description: The gap Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa has been closed in the Atlanta Falcons quarterback race, according to Yahoo Sports . NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport says the lead Tagovailoa held is gone. Both players will now split first-team reps to settle the starting job. The competition is wide open and the pressure is…
fullText:
The gap Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa has been closed in the Atlanta Falcons quarterback race, according to Yahoo Sports. NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport says the lead Tagovailoa held is gone. Both players will now split first-team reps to settle the starting job. The competition is wide open and the pressure is on for both men.

Tagovailoa started with a huge advantage. He looked great during the offseason while Penix was stuck on the sideline. The organization wanted him to win the job and move forward as the starter. That plan relied on Penix staying injured for a while. But the knee injury healed faster than expected.

Penix needed surgery in the week of November 24, 2025, to address a partially torn ACL in his left knee. Before that hurt knee, he threw for 1,982 yards. He completed 60.1 per cent of his passes. Nine total touchdowns and three interceptions were recorded by him during the 2025 season. Now he is back and ready to fight.

Tagovailoa has not looked as sharp in the preseason. Both in practice and in games, Rapoport noted that he had been inconsistent. The gap that seemed so wide has shrunk to nothing. Rapoport explained that Tagovailoa 'had a big-time lead in this race'. That lead is under serious pressure now.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed the split reps. This move proves the door is open for Penix. Rapoport stated that while he seems to have been practicing better the last couple of days, the door is open for Michael Penix. That quote from Rapoport sums up the whole situation perfectly.

The coach made the call after Penix was cleared for 11-on-11 work. This means the competition can now properly begin. Both players get to show what they can do on the field. No more waiting for the injured guy to catch up. They are both in the mix right now.

Penix knows what he can do. He told reporters that as far as a pocket, he can do everything. He is confident in his skills. The only thing holding him back is his doctor's advice on taking hits. His doctor is still waiting for the point when he is comfortable with him taking hits.

That time is getting closer every day. The Falcons' quarterback decision could soon become much clearer. Fans will see the real difference between these two soon enough. The split reps are the first step in a long battle.

There is plenty at stake for Tagovailoa. He is on a one-year deal. This game could be his only chance to prove he belongs. If he loses the job, he might not have another shot in Atlanta. He needs to show he is the long-term starter in the NFL.

Penix faces his own pressure too. He spent much of training camp working his way back. He cannot afford to waste this opportunity. He needs to reclaim the starting role he appeared set to compete for before his injury. The clock is ticking for both of them.

The original plan was for Penix to rehab his knee and return when healthy. The team hoped he would just give Atlanta another option if a change was needed during the season. Now that plan is dead. The team has to pick one man to lead the offense.

Tagovailoa has struggled during the preseason. Rapoport noted that he had been inconsistent both in practice and in games. The door is open for Michael Penix to walk right in. The Falcons fans will get their answer very soon. The race has reached a boiling point.

title: ‘Transphobes are pathetic’: Transgender golfer not apologizing to ‘deeply unwell’ bigots after run of dominance
description: The role of transgender athletes participating in women’s sports has become one of the biggest debates in the country following Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham’s comments on the matter in an ESPN profile earlier this summer. “I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,'”…
fullText:
The role of transgender athletes participating in women's sports has become one of the biggest debates in the country following Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham's comments on the matter in an ESPN profile earlier this summer.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that,'" Cunningham said. "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

Since Cunningham's initial comments, everyone from sports media members to opposing coaches to the White House has weighed in. Now, the debate has reached Alberta, Canada. Transgender golfers Veronica Ivy and Rachel Elser have won five individual women's golf championships this summer, and aren't apologizing for it.

"To the bigots: stay mad, and get a better hobby," Ivy wrote, according to Outkick. "You're deeply unwell and you're obsessed with harassing a stranger. You're not going to make me stop existing and succeeding. I feel really sorry for you. You have my pity."

Alberta Golf updated its official policy to be more inclusive of all competitors in 2025. The organization's rules read as follows:

"For individuals who have undergone gender reassignment after puberty, the following guidelines will be used: I. Male-to-female transgendered persons, to compete as a female, must submit documentation from a medical practitioner that gender reassignment has been ongoing for at least one year."

They just see that I won some competition–without any checking for what level of competition it was," Ivy told OutSports of her detractors earlier this month. "I went from competing in elite world-level track cycling, though never making the national team or the Olympics, to contesting for age group provincial titles.

"I still haven't cracked the top 10 at the Canadian national mid-amateur championship. I'm just out here trying my best, being a good competitor. Transphobes are pathetic."

Hopefully, both Ivy and Elser will keep competing and living their lives to their fullest.
